headline: Medium risk: shared-output and write-capability overlap could enable prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors; compliance risk is low absent sensitive-data evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls, and nuwa-skill is a research agent with allowlisted egress. A plausible pathway exists if Botpress outputs are copied into nuwa-skill or a shared workspace, letting attacker-controlled content be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred from profiles only, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are pasted or synced into nuwa-skill inputs
IF either agent reads shared files as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable any shared clipboard or workspace between the agents.
Prefix all cross-agent text with a non-executable delimiter.
Require manual review before nuwa-skill acts on Botpress output.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress has network_egress set to none, while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress. No data classes are listed for either agent, so there is no direct evidence of sensitive data flow. A leakage pathway is still plausible if they share files or prompts, but the blast radius appears limited by the absence of documented sensitive data handling.
conditions: IF either agent is given secrets, PHI, or customer data in shared prompts or files
IF nuwa-skill is configured to transmit copied context to external services
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of shared prompts and files.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Review allowlisted destinations for nuwa-skill.
Turn off any automatic context export.
requires-engineering: add data-loss prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, and nuwa-skill can egress to allowlisted endpoints, so there is some overlap in operational change surface. However, neither profile documents filesystem write, git mutation, or shared mutable resources, so a true write-write conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains, but the safer low severity fits the evidence.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory
IF either agent is allowed to modify git state or shared databases
mitigations: Separate their working directories.
Avoid granting both agents write access to the same repo.
Run package installs only in an isolated environment.
Check for lockfiles before concurrent runs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress is a support-oriented agent and nuwa-skill is a research-oriented agent, so a plausible workflow is Botpress generating content that nuwa-skill then reuses. There is no documented verification step or downstream action guardrail in either profile, making it plausible that errors propagate from one agent to the other. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill consumes Botpress output as authoritative input
IF no human or programmatic verification step is inserted between them
mitigations: Require source citations before reuse.
Add a human review step for any transferred facts.
Mark Botpress output as untrusted by default.
Use a checksum or schema check on exchanged data.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Neither profile lists data classes touched, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies, so no compliance mismatch is evidenced. Botpress is open-source and nuwa-skill is open-source, but that alone does not establish a residency or regulatory breach pathway. With no sensitive-data or policy evidence, the compliance pathway is not provable.
conditions: IF future configuration assigns regulated data classes to either agent
IF residency or retention policies are later introduced and conflict
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents.
Record residency and retention settings.
Avoid routing regulated data through either agent.
Review vendor terms before deployment.
